title: Hausdorff measure is at most the liminf of covering sums with empty pieces discarded
statement: Let X be an extended metric space whose measurable structure is its Borel σ-algebra, let d ∈ ℝ, let s ⊆ X be arbitrary, let r : ℕ → [0, ∞] with r_k → 0, and let T_{k,i} ⊆ X (k, i ∈ ℕ) satisfy ediam T_{k,i} ≤ r_k for all k, i and s ⊆ ⋃_i T_{k,i} for every k. Then μH[d](s) ≤ liminf_{k→∞} Σ_i ⨆_{T_{k,i} ≠ ∅} (ediam T_{k,i})^d, where μH[d] is Mathlib's unnormalized Hausdorff measure (outer measure on arbitrary sets) and the supremum over the proposition T_{k,i} ≠ ∅ makes empty pieces contribute 0.
lean_statement: ∀ (X : Type) [EMetricSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] (d : ℝ) (s : Set X) (r : ℕ → ℝ≥0∞) (T : ℕ → ℕ → Set X), Tendsto r atTop (𝓝 0) → (∀ k i, ediam (T k i) ≤ r k) → (∀ k, s ⊆ ⋃ i, T k i) → (μH[d] : Measure X) s ≤ liminf (fun k => ∑' i, ⨆ (_ : (T k i).Nonempty), ediam (T k i) ^ d) atTop
